verdict.rationale: Buzz exposes a broad programmatic surface. Its relay speaks the open Nostr protocol (NIP-29/NIP-42), and an official CLI and agent skill cover messaging, channels, DMs, workflows, repos, canvas, feed, reactions, uploads and agent memory, so agents can do most of what humans do. However, full UI parity is never stated or verified: agent creation via CLI stops at a draft that needs owner review in the Desktop app, there is no machine-readable API spec, and the protocol extensions are only draft NIPs. Missing for 10: an explicit, verified statement of full UI/API parity, a machine-readable API specification, headless completion of agent creation without the Desktop review step, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: open repos, send patches, review code, run workflows, edit canvases, orchestrate other agents, drop into voice huddles, create channels
Third-party Nostr clients connect directly to buzz-relay using NIP-29 and NIP-42 authentication
relay operations: owner-reviewed agent drafts, messaging, channels, DMs, users, workflows, feed, reactions, canvas, social, repos, uploads, and agent memory
